active.title: Tennis at Sportime Amagansett
active.description: Book an early court at the East End's best outdoor tennis facility and play a set while the dew is still on the surface and the day belongs to you.
active.bonus: Challenge a stranger warming up on the next court to a tiebreaker set — winner owes nothing, loser buys the post-match coffee.

active.title: Open-Water Swim at Two Mile Hollow Beach
active.description: East Hampton's locals-only stretch of coastline is where serious swimmers do their open-water training in some of the cleanest Atlantic water on Long Island.
active.bonus: Swim parallel to shore past three lifeguard stands without stopping — if the current runs against you, it counts double.

active.title: Bike the Poxabogue Greenway to Wainscott
active.description: The back-road bike route from Bridgehampton through Poxabogue pond to Wainscott Beach is the flattest, most satisfying 10-mile ride on the East End.
active.bonus: Complete the entire route without unclipping — no stopping, no foot on ground — and swim in the ocean at the finish as your reward.

social.title: Late Night at Surf Lodge Montauk
social.description: Montauk's most famous venue plants you barefoot in the sand at a live music night that runs from acoustic sets to full-on dance floor without breaking a sweat.
social.bonus: Dance on the sand directly in front of the stage for at least one full song — no phone out, no self-consciousness, all in.

social.title: Happy Hour on the Dock at The Harbor Bar at Baron's Cove
social.description: Sag Harbor's most social dock bar puts you directly over the water at golden hour with the entire marina as your backdrop.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger at the bar to a game of liar's dice — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Sunday Brunch at Tutto Il Giorno
social.description: Sag Harbor's waterfront Italian brings a downtown Manhattan crowd to a Peconic Bay terrace where the people-watching is as good as the tagliolini.
social.bonus: Start a conversation with the table next to you by asking them to recommend one dish — stay in conversation long enough to actually order it.

social.title: Friday Night at The Stephen Talkhouse
social.description: Amagansett's legendary roadhouse has hosted everyone from Billy Joel to Iggy Pop in a room with no bad spots — show up at 10pm and see who's on.
social.bonus: Get to the front of the crowd within three songs of the headliner starting — no shoving, just timing.

chill.title: Wine and Twilight at Wölffer Estate Vineyard
chill.description: Sagaponack's most beautiful vineyard pours estate rosé on a terrace overlooking rows of vines as the light goes amber — this is what summer in the Hamptons actually looks like.
chill.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pour you something you can't pronounce — then guess the grape variety before they tell you.

chill.title: Afternoon at Parrish Art Museum
chill.description: Water Mill's Herzog & de Meuron barn holds one of the great collections of East End art in an airy, honest building that matches its landscape.
chill.bonus: Find the single work in the collection that moves you most, sit in front of it for ten uninterrupted minutes, and write one sentence about why.

chill.title: Sunset at Camp Hero State Park Bluffs
chill.description: Montauk's decommissioned radar station sits on cliffs above the Atlantic with unobstructed 180-degree sunsets that routinely stop traffic.
chill.bonus: Put your phone away for the entire duration of sunset — not airplane mode, fully in your bag — and just watch it go down.

chill.title: Read at the East Hampton Library Garden
chill.description: A hidden courtyard garden behind one of the most beautiful public libraries on the East Coast delivers total stillness two blocks from Main Street.
chill.bonus: Pick a book off the shelf you know nothing about, sit in the garden, and commit to reading the first 50 pages before you leave.

foodie.title: Early Breakfast at Candy Kitchen
foodie.description: Bridgehampton's Greek-diner time capsule has served the same chrome-counter breakfast since 1956 — eggs, coffee, and zero pretension.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter, order off-menu by describing exactly what you want — if they make it without hesitation, you've found a local.

foodie.title: Dinner at Nick & Toni's
foodie.description: East Hampton's most enduring power-dinner room serves wood-roasted everything to a crowd that has been coming here for decades — and looks like it.
foodie.bonus: Identify one genuinely famous person in the room — then send them a drink without revealing who it's from.

foodie.title: Farm Stand Crawl on Sagg Main Street
foodie.description: Sagaponack's single-lane farm road is lined with honor-system stands selling just-picked corn, tomatoes, and flowers that redefine what produce should taste like.
foodie.bonus: Buy something from every stand you pass without spending more than $20 total — then build a meal from what you've collected.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Calissa
foodie.description: Water Mill's upscale Greek taverna plates whole branzino and proper loukoumades in a whitewashed setting that earns every dollar of its price tag.
foodie.bonus: Order a dish entirely in Greek — ask your server what it's called and pronounce it back to them before they put in the order.

foodie.title: Lunch at The Lobster Roll (LUNCH)
foodie.description: A Route 27 institution since 1965, the cold mayo lobster roll here is the definitive Hamptons summer meal — order it at the window, eat at a picnic table.
foodie.bonus: Order the lobster roll with no modifications and eat it before you sit down — standing at the counter is how regulars do it.

adventure.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard Sagg Pond to the Atlantic
adventure.description: Sagaponack's hidden pond connects to the ocean through a narrow channel that delivers a genuinely wild open-water moment.
adventure.bonus: Cross the sandbar channel into open Atlantic water on your board — if a wave knocks you off, you have to swim the board back before remounting.

adventure.title: Cliff Scramble at Shadmoor State Park
adventure.description: Montauk's bluff trails drop you onto a wild, boulder-strewn beach that feels nothing like the manicured Hamptons everyone else visits.
adventure.bonus: Scramble down to the beach without using the main path — find the unofficial bluff descent and make it down without using your hands.

adventure.title: Kayak the Mashomack Preserve on Shelter Island
adventure.description: 2,000 acres of tidal creeks and osprey-dotted marshland make this the most underrated paddle in the Hamptons ecosystem.
adventure.bonus: Navigate into one tidal creek so narrow the reeds brush both sides of your kayak — if you can touch the shore without tipping, it counts.

adventure.title: Sunrise Surf at Ditch Plains Beach
adventure.description: Montauk's most beloved break delivers consistent waves at dawn when the crowds are gone and the Atlantic turns gold.
adventure.bonus: Catch a wave, ride it all the way to shore, and then go back out immediately — no celebrating on the beach until you've done it twice.
